proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}
 =\{((r_{bt}),(q_w))\in\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}.             \tag{1}
\]
By the premise, \(\mathsf P(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge 1-\alpha\).  Work on this event.  Because the observable law is admitted by \(\mathfrak M_H\), the converse in \(\text{thm:causal-response-tree-lift}\) and \(\text{lem:triple-projection-and-extension}\) imply \(\Gamma_H(p,q)\ne\varnothing\).  Fix \(x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)\) and define
\[
 r^\circ_{bt}=\pi p_{bt},\qquad
 s^\circ_w=\pi q_w,\qquad
 x^\circ_{bw}=\pi x_{bw}.                                \tag{2}
\]
Landmark-survival positivity gives \(\pi>0\), while probability normalization gives
\[
 \sum_{b,t}r^\circ_{bt}=\pi\le 1.                         \tag{3}
\]
Membership in the event (1) gives the cellwise constraints on \(r^\circ\), and, because \(s^\circ_w=q_w\sum_{b,t}r^\circ_{bt}\),
\[
 \underline q_w\sum_{b,t}r^\circ_{bt}
 \le s^\circ_w
 \le \overline q_w\sum_{b,t}r^\circ_{bt}                 \tag{4}
\]
for every \(w\in\mathbb I_H\).  The row equations, column equations, and support restriction in \(\Gamma_H(p,q)\) give
\[
 \sum_wx^\circ_{bw}=\pi p_b=\sum_t r^\circ_{bt},\qquad
 \sum_bx^\circ_{bw}=\pi q_w=s^\circ_w,\qquad
 x^\circ_{bw}=0\quad\text{if }b+w>H.                    \tag{5}
\]
Together with nonnegativity, (2)--(5) prove
\[
 (\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ,\mathbf x^\circ)
 \in\widehat{\mathcal P}_{n,\alpha}.                    \tag{6}
\]
This argument holds for every \(x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)\).  The corresponding image coordinate is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{b<m,t}t r^\circ_{bt}+\sum_{b\ge m,w}w x^\circ_{bw}
 &=\pi\left(\sum_{b<m,t}t p_{bt}+\sum_{b\ge m,w}w x_{bw}\right)\\
 &=\pi\left(\sum_{b<m}\mu_b+\sum_{b\ge m,w}w x_{bw}\right).
 \end{aligned}                                            \tag{7}
\]
By \(\text{thm:joint-value-set-and-support}\), as \(x\) ranges over \(\Gamma_H(p,q)\), the vector in (7) ranges over the entire sharp causal identified set.  Equations (6)--(7) therefore yield
\[
 \mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}.                  \tag{8}
\]

For deterministic optimizer coverage, positivity of \(\pi\) makes the scaling map bijective:
\[
 \mathsf X_H(\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ)
 =\{\pi x:x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)\}.                          \tag{9}
\]
Indeed, one inclusion follows from the equations in (5), and the reverse inclusion follows by dividing every candidate plan by \(\pi>0\).  Substitution into \(\mathsf J_m\) and then into its transport optimum gives, simultaneously for every \(m,j\in\mathcal M\),
\[
 \mathsf D_{mj}(\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ)=D_{mj},
 \qquad
 \mathsf R_m(\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ)=R_m.       \tag{10}
\]
The true margin pair belongs to the projection of the confidence polytope by (6).  Hence
\[
 \underline R_m^{n,\alpha}\le R_m\le\overline R_m^{n,\alpha}
 \quad\text{for every }m\in\mathcal M.                  \tag{11}
\]
If \(m\in\mathcal M^\star\), then \(R_m=\min_jR_j\), and (11) gives
\[
 \underline R_m^{n,\alpha}
 \le R_m
 =\min_{j\in\mathcal M}R_j
 \le\min_{j\in\mathcal M}\overline R_j^{n,\alpha}.     \tag{12}
\]
Thus \(m\in\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\), proving
\[
 \mathcal M^\star\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}.                  \tag{13}
\]
No step makes a Hall inequality or regret comparison strict, so (8) and (13) remain valid on Hall faces and retain every tied deterministic minimizer.

On the event (1), (6) shows that the confidence polytope is nonempty.  It is closed and bounded: all its coordinates are nonnegative, its total row mass is at most one, and its row and column equations bound every \(s_w\) and \(x_{bw}\) by that total mass.  Hence it and its coordinate projections are compact polytopes, including candidate points of total mass zero.  The value confidence set is a linear image of this polytope.  For fixed candidate margins and each \((m,j)\), \(\mathsf D_{mj}\) is the optimum of the explicitly constrained finite transport program over \(\mathsf X_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)\); the regret takes a maximum over the finite menu, and its envelopes optimize this finite-dimensional value over the displayed compact projection.  Thus all reported sets and envelopes are computable finite-dimensional optimization objects.  Taking probabilities in (8) and (13) proves both inclusions with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).

added_lemmas.statement: If \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\) covers \((r_{bt},q_w)\) simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), then with the same probability \(\Delta^\star\subseteq\widehat{\Delta}_{n,\alpha}\).  This inclusion retains every randomized minimizer without requiring uniqueness, strict Hall slack, or regret separation.  For candidate margins of total mass \(\tau\), \(\mathsf R_{\mathbf r,\mathbf s}\) is \(H\tau\)-Lipschitz on \(\Delta_{\mathcal M}\) in \(\ell^1\), and the two confidence envelopes are \(H\)-Lipschitz; consequently \(\widehat{\Delta}_{n,\alpha}\) is closed and is computable by finite-dimensional transport-support optimization.  Moreover, when \(H=3\) and \(\mathcal M=\{1,2,3\}\), there are two triangular law sequences in \(\mathfrak M_H\) whose \(n\)-sample observed-data laws have total variation \(o(1)\), such that the first has the unique randomized optimizer \(e_3\) and the second has the unique randomized optimizer \((9/16,5/16,1/8)\).  Therefore, for \(0<\alpha<1/2\), every uniformly honest observed-data outer confidence region for \(\Delta^\star\) has a law sequence along which it contains both points with limiting lower probability at least \(1-2\alpha\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
First prove the finite-sample inclusion.  Work on the simultaneous first-stage event \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) in (1) of the proof of \(\text{thm:confidence-polytope}\), and put
\[
 \mathbf r^\circ=(\pi p_{bt})_{b,t},\qquad
 \mathbf s^\circ=(\pi q_w)_w.                            \tag{1}
\]
That proof shows \((\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ)\in\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}\).  Moreover, by \(\pi>0\), its scaling identity (9) and value identity (7) give
\[
 \mathsf V_H(\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ)
 =\mathcal V(p_{BT},q).                                  \tag{2}
\]
Consequently \(h_{\mathsf V_H(\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ)}=h_{\mathcal V}\), and the support representation in \(\text{thm:randomized-minimax-regret}\) yields
\[
 \mathsf R_{\mathbf r^\circ,\mathbf s^\circ}(\delta)
 =\max_{j\in\mathcal M}h_{\mathcal V}(\delta-e_j)
 =\mathcal R(\delta)                                    \tag{3}
\]
for every \(\delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}\).  Thus the true candidate margins are one of the margin pairs over which both envelopes range, and
\[
 \underline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)
 \le\mathcal R(\delta)
 \le\overline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)             \tag{4}
\]
simultaneously for all \(\delta\).  If \(\delta^\star\in\Delta^\star\), then
\[
 \underline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta^\star)
 \le\mathcal R(\delta^\star)
 =\inf_{\lambda\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}}\mathcal R(\lambda)
 \le\inf_{\lambda\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}}
      \overline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\lambda).         \tag{5}
\]
The defining inequality therefore puts every \(\delta^\star\) in \(\widehat{\Delta}_{n,\alpha}\).  Since the event has probability at least \(1-\alpha\), this proves the asserted simultaneous coverage, including all ties.

We next give the promised Lipschitz and computability details.  For candidate margins let
\[
 \tau=\sum_{b,t}r_{bt}=\sum_ws_w.
\]
Every \(\mathbf x\in\mathsf X_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)\) has total mass \(\tau\).  Since \(0\le t,w\le H\), the two row sets in the definition of \(\mathsf J_m\) are disjoint and exhaust a subset of the total row mass, whence
\[
 0\le \mathsf J_m(\mathbf r,\mathbf x)\le H\tau
 \quad(m\in\mathcal M).                                 \tag{6}
\]
It follows directly from the support definition that, for all \(\lambda,\lambda'\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal M|}\),
\[
 \left|h_{\mathsf V_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)}(\lambda)
       -h_{\mathsf V_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)}(\lambda')\right|
 \le H\tau\,\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_1.                    \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the left side is at most \(\sup_{v\in\mathsf V_H}|(\lambda-\lambda')^\top v|\), and (6) bounds every coordinate of \(v\) by \(H\tau\).  The elementary inequality \(|\max_j a_j-\max_j a'_j|\le\max_j|a_j-a'_j|\) and (7) now imply
\[
 |\mathsf R_{\mathbf r,\mathbf s}(\delta)
   -\mathsf R_{\mathbf r,\mathbf s}(\delta')|
 \le H\tau\,\|\delta-\delta'\|_1.                      \tag{8}
\]
Every pair in \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}\) has \(0\le\tau\le1\).  Taking an infimum or a supremum of a family with the common Lipschitz constant \(H\) preserves that constant, so both envelopes are \(H\)-Lipschitz.  The simplex is compact; hence the infimum of the upper envelope over it is attained, and its weak sublevel inequality makes \(\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}\) closed.  Finally, \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}\) is the projection of the explicitly constrained finite polytope, each support value is a finite transport linear program over \(\mathsf X_H\), and only finitely many comparators are maximized.  Thus the envelopes and the outer set are finite-dimensional optimization objects; no differentiability or active-face stability is used.

It remains to prove the uniform obstruction.  Fix \(H=3\), \(\mathcal M=\{1,2,3\}\), and the common \((p,q)\) margins of \(\mathsf E_3\).  Their nontrivial Hall slacks are strictly positive, so \(\Gamma_3(p,q)\ne\varnothing\).  For law zero set \(T=0\) in every row.  Then \(\mu_b=0\) for all \(b\).  Capacity forces row \(b=3\) into column \(w=0\), so every compatible value vector satisfies
\[
 J_3=0,
 \qquad J_1\ge0,
 \qquad J_2\ge0.                                        \tag{9}
\]
Therefore \(\mathcal R(e_3)=0\).  To prove uniqueness, consider the feasible plan whose nonzero cells are
\[
 x_{00}=\frac15,\quad x_{03}=\frac15,\quad
 x_{11}=\frac1{10},\quad x_{12}=\frac15,\quad
 x_{21}=\frac15,\quad x_{30}=\frac1{10}.                 \tag{10}
\]
Its row and column sums are the displayed \(p\) and \(q\) margins of \(\mathsf E_3\), and every listed cell obeys \(b+w\le3\).  Under law zero it generates
\[
 (J_1,J_2,J_3)=\left(\frac7{10},\frac15,0\right).        \tag{11}
\]
For any \(\delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}\), comparison with threshold three at this same latent law gives
\[
 \mathcal R(\delta)
 \ge \frac7{10}\delta_1+\frac15\delta_2.                \tag{12}
\]
The right side is positive unless \(\delta=e_3\).  Equations (9)--(12) prove that law zero has the unique randomized optimizer \(e_3\).

For law one, retain the same \((p,q)\) margins.  Conditional on \(B=1\), put probabilities \(5/6\) and \(1/6\) on \(T=1\) and \(T=2\), respectively; conditional on \(B=2\), put probabilities \(1/8\) and \(7/8\) on \(T=0\) and \(T=1\); set \(T=0\) in rows zero and three.  Multiplication by the row masses gives
\[
 (\mu_0,\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3)
 =\left(0,\frac7{20},\frac7{40},0\right),               \tag{13}
\]
so this is the value geometry of \(\mathsf E_3\).  The exact calculation in \(\text{thm:randomized-minimax-regret}\) proves that its unique randomized optimizer is
\[
 \delta^\star=\left(\frac9{16},\frac5{16},\frac18\right). \tag{14}
\]

We now realize these two summary laws as nearly indistinguishable observed-data laws.  In both, randomize baseline treatment with probability \(1/2\), use no death, set \(S_k^0=S_k^1=1\), use the same pre-landmark intensive paths realizing the common \(B\) margin, and use the same standard-arm sustained paths realizing the common \(q\) margin.  Choose any feasible capped coupling, extend it to a triple coupling by \(\text{lem:triple-projection-and-extension}\), and use the cap-fibre construction in \(\text{thm:causal-response-tree-lift}\) to complete the switched and unused branches.  The resulting raw paths are nonnegative-integer valued, death is absorbing, and the construction enforces both capped residual transportability and \(B+W\le3\).  Independently of the response tree and assignment, observe every subject through \(k\), continue observation through \(K\) with probability
\[
 \varepsilon_n=n^{-2}>0,                                \tag{15}
\]
and otherwise censor at \(k\).  Thus baseline assignment, landmark survival, and every factual at-risk censoring continuation probability are positive.  Independence in (15) gives the arm-specific censoring-exchangeability equality.  Hence both triangular sequences lie in \(\mathfrak M_H\).

Couple one observation from the two sequences using the same assignment, censoring draw, pre-landmark history, and standard-arm history.  The observations can differ only if \(R=1\) and follow-up continues through \(K\), an event of probability \(\varepsilon_n/2\).  Coordinatewise coupling of \(n\) observations and the union bound therefore give
\[
 \left\|P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}-P_{1,n}^{\otimes n}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \frac{n\varepsilon_n}{2}
 =\frac1{2n}\longrightarrow0.                           \tag{16}
\]

Let \(\mathcal C_n\) be any observed-data outer confidence region satisfying
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathsf P\in\mathfrak M_H}
 \mathsf P^{\otimes n}\{\Delta^\star(\mathsf P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}
 \ge1-\alpha.                                           \tag{17}
\]
Applied to the two triangular sequences, (17) gives coverage of \(e_3\) under law zero and of \(\delta^\star\) under law one, each with probability at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\).  Total variation in (16) transfers the latter event to law zero at a cost \(o(1)\).  A union bound under law zero yields
\[
 P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}\{e_3,\delta^\star\in\mathcal C_n\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1).                                     \tag{18}
\]
Taking the lower limit proves the final assertion.  The two laws have strict Hall slack and unique, separated randomized optimizers; the obstruction is solely the vanishing post-landmark observation probability permitted by pointwise censoring positivity.
added_lemmas.justification: The same first-stage margin event must cover all mixed minimax rules, while the explicit Lipschitz and two-point results delimit what this inversion can achieve under pointwise overlap.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing deterministic optimizer inversion does not cover mixtures on the policy simplex or expose the vanishing-information obstruction for randomized optimizers.
added_lemmas.consumer: A capped switching analysis can report an outer region for every randomized minimax rule, including tied mixtures, while recognizing that pointwise censoring positivity alone cannot make that region shrink uniformly.

proposed.construction:
Put \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}=\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf r,\mathbf s}\widehat{\mathcal P}_{n,\alpha}\).  For \((\mathbf r,\mathbf s)\in\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}\), define
\[
 \mathsf V_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)
 =\{(\mathsf J_m(\mathbf r,\mathbf x))_{m\in\mathcal M}:
       \mathbf x\in\mathsf X_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)\},
 \qquad
 h_{\mathsf V_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)}(\lambda)
 =\max_{v\in\mathsf V_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)}\lambda^\top v,
\]
and
\[
 \mathsf R_{\mathbf r,\mathbf s}(\delta)
 =\max_{j\in\mathcal M}
   h_{\mathsf V_H(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)}(\delta-e_j),
 \qquad \delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}.
\]
When \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}\ne\varnothing\), set
\[
 \underline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)
 =\inf_{(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)\in\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}}
      \mathsf R_{\mathbf r,\mathbf s}(\delta),
 \qquad
 \overline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)
 =\sup_{(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)\in\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}}
      \mathsf R_{\mathbf r,\mathbf s}(\delta),
\]
and define the randomized-optimizer outer set by
\[
 \widehat{\Delta}_{n,\alpha}
 =\left\{\delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}:
   \underline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)
   \le \inf_{\lambda\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}}
          \overline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\lambda)\right\}.
\]
If \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{n,\alpha}=\varnothing\), use the total convention \(\underline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)=0\), \(\overline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)=H\), and \(\widehat{\Delta}_{n,\alpha}=\Delta_{\mathcal M}\).

prose_updates.tldr: A randomized recurrent-event trial identifies separately capped baseline and residual margins while leaving their dependence unknown, and the raw recurrent paths remain unbounded. The externally prespecified sensitivity restriction \(B+W\le H\) creates a Ferrers transport problem and is not implied by separate capping. Dahl2008, Theorem 4, supplies only the reindexed staircase feasibility support. The cap-fibre response-tree construction proves that every feasible triple coupling preserves the observed law and is attainable even after imposing the published uncapped residual no-carry-over equality. The resulting sharp endpoints and common-law value polytope yield exact deterministic and randomized minimax regret; in the cap-three witness the unique randomized rule \((9/16,5/16,1/8)\) has regret \(17/160\), strictly below the best deterministic regret \(7/40\), while scalar intervals select a different deterministic threshold. One confidence-polytope inversion covers the whole value set and every deterministic or randomized robust optimizer at Hall, policy, and mixture ties. Uniformly shrinking censoring-adjusted inference is impossible under the frozen pointwise-overlap assumptions: in the cap-three two-point experiment, any uniformly honest randomized-optimizer region must contain both \(e_3\) and \((9/16,5/16,1/8)\) with limiting lower probability at least \(1-2\alpha\). A constructive efficient procedure under quantitative overlap and nuisance-rate conditions remains open.

project_justification.gap: The closest recurrent-event switching analysis supplies a published uncapped no-carry-over equality, threshold-wise scalar sharp bounds, and deterministic decision criteria. Dahl2008, Theorem 4, separately settles staircase fixed-margin feasibility. Neither line proves that every capped coupling has an observed-law-preserving cap-fibre lift within the published raw-no-carry-over subclass, identifies the common latent value law across a threshold menu, computes deterministic and randomized minimax regret, or supplies confidence inversion for the full deterministic and randomized optimizer correspondences together with a sharp vanishing-information limitation.
project_justification.fill: The formal kernel combines the attributed Dahl2008 feasibility certificate with an explicit raw-path cap-fibre lift, proves sharp transfer to the published uncapped no-carry-over subclass intersected with the capacity restriction, derives atom-correct endpoints and the common-coupling value polytope, computes deterministic and randomized regret with the eligibility-greedy support oracle, supplies the exact cap-three reversal and unique optimal mixture, and gives simultaneous confidence-polytope inversion for the whole value set and both optimizer correspondences. An explicit cap-three two-law experiment proves that pointwise censoring positivity alone cannot support uniformly shrinking randomized-optimizer inference.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite vectors \((r_{bt},q_w)\) are identified under factual-arm sequential coarsening at random and may be estimated with censoring adjustment. Their simultaneous confidence region feeds one perspective polytope whose images cover the whole value set and all deterministic and randomized minimax rules without excluding Hall or policy ties. Under the frozen pointwise-positivity class, uniformly shrinking inference is impossible, including for randomized optimizers. A constructive cross-fitted procedure remains open only after adding quantitative effective assignment, survival, and censoring overlap together with explicit nuisance-rate and second-order remainder conditions.

prose_updates.related_work: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 Assumption 1 supplies the uncapped residual no-carry-over equality, while Proposition 1 and the decision section supply threshold-wise scalar sharp bounds and deterministic regime logic. The cap-fibre construction here shows that, after intersecting with the externally prespecified restriction \(B+W\le H\), every feasible capped coupling remains attainable in that published raw-no-carry-over subclass; the new content is therefore the capacity-constrained backward-deficit endpoint, common-law value, and deterministic and randomized regret geometry, not a retreat to a different causal class. Strassen1965 gives the general support-constrained coupling principle. More directly, Dahl2008, Theorem 4 and Section 3, already characterize fixed-margin staircase feasibility and constructions; after reversing the row order, the antidiagonal Hall criterion is exactly that specialization and is not claimed as new. ZhangRichardson2025 motivates separate treatment of weak and strict events for discrete sums. HoffmanVeinott1993 informs the staircase greedy argument, which is used here as a specialized support oracle rather than freestanding algorithmic novelty. RichardsonRobins2013 supplies FFRCISTG semantics, and GreseleEtAl2022 frames the local-to-global causal-marginal obstruction resolved by the observed-law-preserving lift. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026 shows the decision relevance of joint payoff geometry and randomization; the present geometry is the image of one capped transport law. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, AndrewsSoares2010, and Gafarov2025 inform confidence inversion at binding inequalities and changing faces. The randomized envelope inversion here is set-theoretic and remains valid at mixture ties, while its two-point limit makes explicit why pointwise overlap does not imply uniform shrinkage. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 supports factual-arm sequential coarsening identification.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The primitive counts are raw, nonnegative-integer-valued, and not globally bounded by \(H\). The condition \(B+W\le H\) constrains the separately capped prefix burden and switched residual and remains a substantive sensitivity restriction. The cap-fibre lift may draw an uncapped switched residual above \(H\) when \(W=H\); this is essential for preserving the published uncapped standard residual law and is why the theorem asserts equality only after capping. A finite-reserve mechanism gives a compatible class, but no such mechanism or clinically defensible cap has been established for SPRINT. Dahl's feasibility criterion can reject a proposed cap statistically but cannot establish clinical credibility. The response-tree theorem preserves the original arm-specific sequential censoring law on factual at-risk histories and does not assume independence between censoring and the entire cross-world response tree. Finally, pointwise censoring positivity permits vanishing-information sequences. The negative uniform-inference results therefore rule out uniformly shrinking confidence regions for the whole value set and for either deterministic or randomized optimizer correspondences under the frozen class; constructive efficient inference requires additional quantitative overlap and nuisance-remainder conditions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved scope consists of atom-correct endpoints, a raw-path cap-fibre causal lift preserving factual-arm sequential censoring, exact sharp transfer to the published uncapped residual no-carry-over subclass intersected with \(B+W\le H\), the complete common-law value and support characterization, deterministic and randomized minimax regret, the rational recommendation reversal and unique optimal mixture, and confidence-polytope inversion for the whole value set and all deterministic and randomized robust optimizers, including Hall and policy ties. The candidate randomized regret is explicitly \(H\tau\)-Lipschitz in the policy mixture at total candidate mass \(\tau\). Dahl2008, Theorem 4, is used only as attributed feasibility support. Uniform inference is resolved negatively under the frozen assumptions by vanishing-information witnesses, including a cap-three pair forcing every uniformly honest randomized-optimizer region to contain both \(e_3\) and \((9/16,5/16,1/8)\) with limiting lower probability at least \(1-2\alpha\). A nonvacuous cross-fitted or efficient construction under explicit quantitative assignment, survival, censoring-overlap, and nuisance-rate conditions remains open. SPRINT is only a conditional capped-loss consumer: a mechanism and cap must be justified externally and prespecified at \(k=300\), and the application is rejected if no credible capacity interpretation exists or the censoring-adjusted Hall confidence system is infeasible.

statement_notes.consumer: A capped switching analysis can use this common first-stage perspective polytope to cover every compatible value vector and deterministic robust threshold; the randomized-confidence theorem applies the same object to all mixed minimax rules.

statement_notes.justification: The same first-stage event covers every randomized minimizer by lower-versus-upper regret envelopes, while the explicit Lipschitz bound and two-point witness delimit uniform informativeness.
statement_notes.gap: Neither scalar endpoint inversion nor deterministic optimizer coverage addresses the policy simplex, randomized ties, or the possibility that two unique mixed optimizers are observationally indistinguishable under vanishing censoring overlap.
statement_notes.consumer: A robust capped switching analysis can report all mixed minimax rules compatible with the first-stage region and must disclose when pointwise overlap prevents that region from shrinking uniformly.
